definitions.gloss: tart (open pastry with sweet or savory filling)
definitions.explanation: A baked dish consisting of a shortcrust or pâte sablée base filled with cream, custard, fruit, jam, or savory ingredients. From French "tarte"; in Japan, the dessert version (especially fruit tarts) is most familiar.

examples.japanese: イチゴのタルトを{食|た}べた。
{母|はは}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}にタルトを{焼|や}いた。
examples.english: I baked a tart for my mother's birthday.

examples.japanese: ケーキ{屋|や}さんには、{季節|きせつ}のフルーツを{使|つか}ったタルトが{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: At the cake shop, tarts made with seasonal fruits were lined up in the display.

examples.japanese: サクサクの{生地|きじ}に{滑|なめ}らかなカスタードクリームをのせ、{上|うえ}にイチジクを{飾|かざ}って{完成|かんせい}したタルトは、{見|み}た{目|め}も{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: Topped with smooth custard cream on a flaky crust and decorated with figs, the finished tart was beautiful to look at as well.

notes:
タルト is a loanword from French tarte, referring to an open pastry typically with a sweet filling. In Japan, the term is most often associated with elegant fruit and custard desserts sold at patisseries and cafes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- タルトを{焼|や}く: to bake a tart
- タルトを{作|つく}る: to make a tart
- フルーツタルト: fruit tart
- イチゴのタルト: strawberry tart
- レモンタルト: lemon tart
- チョコレートタルト: chocolate tart
- タルト{生地|きじ}: tart shell / tart dough

SIMILAR WORDS:
- パイ: pie — typically has a top crust as well
- ケーキ: cake — sponge-based, distinct category
- キッシュ: quiche — savory tart with egg-and-cream filling
- フィナンシェ / マドレーヌ: small French cakes (different category)

CULTURAL NOTE:
- 「{愛媛|えひめ}{銘菓|めいか}{一六|いちろく}タルト」 is a famous {愛媛|えひめ} regional confection that is technically a kind of jelly-roll cake, named tarte from a historical loanword usage; it is unrelated to the modern Western tart.
- French-style fruit tarts are a typical Western-cake-shop offering and a popular gift.
